featured_reviews.review_text: After many years visited this fabulous steak joint. Loved the sizzler - quality of the meat, the taste was just fabulous . I would definitely recommend steak/sizzler lovers who have been here, a must visit. Keep it going, Team Gondola! Best Wishes!

featured_reviews.name: Asad Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
It's a nice little restaurant for a cosy evening or dinner outing with a small group of friends or a date. The place is small so not suitable for a huge group because of its size and popularity. There's always a good number of people waiting so expect a waiting time of at least half an hour during weekends.

The restaurant is most famous for its beef burgers and sizzler platters which have a distinct style of cooking that makes it flavoursome. There are other options as well, there are chicken and mutton dishes as well which are equally good. The food is not spicy so if that's the taste one prefers prior request is necessary. The soup was pretty good as well and so were the starters. The restaurant scores pretty well in taste and food quality.

The service is the area which needs little improvement because the staff felt too less compared to the crowd which slowed the speed of service significantly. The staff was very occupied and therefore wasn't able to pay attention to any other requests which were understandable but it's nothing that cannot be solved.

In terms of pricing, it's an expensive place but with good quality food, taste and quantity. If you're someone who likes beef dishes and sizzlers then it's the place you should check out.

featured_reviews.name: Tanya Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text: Honestly, I was waiting to eat here since I don’t live in Mumbai anymore. Went there as it was my aunts birthday and decided to order what it was really famous for. A steak sizzler. Sorry but my reason for 2 stars is simply cause I missed seeing veggies in the sizzler. It was loaded with fried rice and my steak was hiding somewhere below. I had to search for it. The steak was very well done. And the rice had a lot of soda in it. It disgusted me eating there for the first time. Sorry gondola u guys have lost the meaning of a sizzler to me. Pls keep carbs less. Add more veggies

featured_reviews.name: John Dsouza
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited GONDOLA in Bandra today with great expectations for we had heard a lot about this place.

We first ordered a 'Crispy Honey Paneer'. What arrived was 'Crispy Honey CHICKEN'. We had to return it.

I ordered a a 'Medium Rare steak' with veggies, mashed potatoes & Mushroom sauce.

I got a FLATTENED PIECE OF MEAT, 'HEAVILY OVER DONE' with FRENCH FRIES, and vegetables which were overcooked and doused in oil and Soy sauce (obviously they were made for sizzlers and the lazy COOK served them with a Steak). The Mushroom sauce was a disgrace, it was a white sauce (not Brown), hinting that there was ZERO STOCK, WINE AND OTHER INGREDIENTS USED as it should've been. It was a shameful mix of Cream and diced Mushrooms, which tasted Horribly bland (not a grain of salt in it).

I returned it, for I do not like to eat meat that is over cooked like burnt leather.

Requested the order taker to PLEASE get me a proper thick piece of MEDIUM RARE steak....I advised him to tell the 'Chef' to cook it for 3 to 5 minutes each side which will do the trick.

The waiter came back with the same bed of stir fried vegetables, but this time had a decent 1 inch thick Sirloin on it. Made me happy. But my happiness was short lived, for when I cut the meat, it turned out to be a RARE. It was just lightly seared for about 1mm on the outside and TOTALLY RAW INSIDE.

As I did not wish to be infected with Gastrointestinal disease by eating raw meat, obviously I complained to the order taker and sent back the steak for the SECOND TIME. This probably frustrated the inexperienced 'COOK' (Cannot insult the Chef's  profession by calling this person who messed up a simple steak and who has NO CLUE about sauces or even about how veggies are served with a steak, a CHEF). He just clobbered the lovely shaped sirloin with a meat tenderizer, FLATTENED IT COMPLETELY and sent it back to me within 1 minute.

I asked the order taker, what kind of 'COOK' he had, who is continously messing up a simple order. The poor order taker  who was doing a wondefdul job and was most courteous, looked visibly embarassed.

Finally, not wanting to take a chance, I accepted the ordertakers suggestion and ordered a Chicken instead. Th chicken which was obviously prepared for a sizzler as it was cooked with all the ingredients used for sizzlers. I was too tired to complain a 4th time, so quietly ate the Chicken, heavily doused in Soy sauce....

It was a horrible night, totaly ruined by a horrible cook, who truly does not belong in a classy place like GONDOLA.

I definitely will never return to GONDOLA, but if the OWNER of GONDOLA gets to read this review, he would be doing his restaurant a favour by FIRING THE HORRIBLE COOK, sobhe does not lose more customers.

Finally, please do not take your customers for granted and serve them anything you feel like to save money. Just because you serve a lot of sizzlers, it does not mean that you serve the vegetables you have pre-prwpared for sizzlers, along with all your dishes.

Reapect your clients, give them their money's worth. If you serve them garbage, like I was served today, you will ultimately not have any customers left to fool.

The service and the attitude of all the wait staff was good. I truly felt bad for the order taker, who was doing a wonderful job, but the COOK let him down with the horrible food.

What a SHAME!!!

featured_reviews.name: Murtaza Anverali
featured_reviews.review_text:
The best of Pan-Asian food has a new address, and it’s unforgettable. From the moment you walk in, the vibe is unique — moody lighting, contemporary Asian-inspired décor, and an energy that feels both upscale and inviting. It’s the kind of place where dinner turns into an experience.

The food is simply awesome. Every dish hits that perfect balance of flavor, texture, and presentation. But the showstopper? The Honey Chilli Prawns. Plump, juicy prawns tossed in a glossy, sticky-sweet glaze with just the right kick of chilli. Crispy on the outside, succulent inside, and dangerously addictive — one bite and you’ll know why it’s a must try.

Service is sharp, portions are generous, and the menu is packed with bold, authentic Pan-Asian flavors done right. If you love food that excites your palate and a vibe that elevates your night, this place deserves a spot on your list. Must visit.

featured_reviews.name: Sweet Sour

The Panda Passion was vibrant and refreshing, while the Martini added the perfect touch of timeless elegance to the table. The Crystal Dumplings were delicate and flavourful, and the Spicy Avocado Sushi brought just the right amount of heat with a smooth, creamy finish.

featured_reviews.review_text: I recently visited this amazing restaurant in Bandra, and it’s an absolute gem for lovers of Asian cuisine. The sushi here is hands down the best I’ve had in the city – fresh, flavorful, and perfectly rolled. Their Thai and Chinese dishes are equally impressive, with authentic taste and balanced spices. Seafood lovers will be in heaven with their wide selection of fresh, well-cooked options. The food presentation is top-notch, making every dish a visual treat before you even take a bite. The ambience is super cute and cozy, perfect for a casual date or dinner with friends. Despite the high quality, the prices are surprisingly reasonable. The service was attentive and friendly, adding to the overall experience. It’s definitely a must-visit spot in Bandra for anyone craving great Asian flavors. I’ll surely be coming back soon!

featured_reviews.name: amin shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
📍 Kuai Kitchen – Khar West, Mumbai
🍱 Location: Shop No. 3/4, Mangal Bhavna, Khar Pali Rd, Khar West, Mumbai 400052
If you're a fan of sushi, dim sum, and pan-Asian cuisine, Kuai Kitchen is the place to be! The ambience here is aesthetic and welcoming, with both indoor and outdoor dining options that make it a perfect spot for a cozy meal or a catch-up with friends.
We started off with some refreshing mocktails — I tried the Martini mocktail, which was super refreshing and full of flavor. My brother went for the Panda Passion, and not only did it taste amazing, but the presentation was on point too!
Here’s what we ordered and absolutely loved:
🍤 Dynamite Prawns – perfectly crispy and packed with flavor.
🥟 Spicy Chicken Dumplings – delicious, with a rich, flavorful filling and great presentation.
🍣 Volcano Prawn Tempura Roll Sushi – visually stunning and tasted just as good as it looked.
🍗 Chicken with Chilli Oil and Spring Onion – bold flavors with a nice kick.
🍚 Blue Butter Japanese Fried Rice (Chicken) – cooked to perfection, flavorful, and unique in taste.
And finally, to end on a sweet note:
🍫 Labubu Chocolate Bao – a warm, gooey dessert bao that was absolutely mouthwatering!
✨ The service was top-notch. The staff were attentive and helpful, and the manager personally guided us through the menu. Every dish was presented beautifully, and the quality was consistent throughout.
💯 Overall: 10/10 Experience
Highly recommended for all lovers of Thai, Asian, sushi, and dim sum. Add this place to your food bucket list — you won't regret it!

featured_reviews.name: aditya mathur
featured_reviews.review_text:
FAKE HYPE. AVOID visit. Very disappointed. Nothing special atall. Just a mediocre pan Asia joint . Lets get straight to it. Came here as i read good reviews online but sadly it was all wrong.
We were a party of 10 who went here on a Saturday night.
Cons :
1. No valet when we arrived. Had to look for parking for 15 mins.
2. Less than enthusiastic staff and thats putting lightly.
3. Small place so getting a seating inside might be difficult.
4. Lotus stem and teriyaki bao were soo sweet that it felt like eating desert. This was conveyed to the management for feedback.
5. Tatse and portion of the dishes do not justify the its cost. Too steep for the kind of mideocre food available.
6. Steamed rice was undercooked and left untouched. We had given up by this time and resorted to looking elsewhere for dinner party 2 .
7. No alcohol. Alcohol would have helped in stuffing down some of the itmes we ordered or atleast numb our taste buds enough to appreciate the food.
Pros :
1. Ambience is neat and cosy.
2. The sushi was very well made and we all enjoyed it.
3. The menu is well curated with good variety of both veg and non veg options.
I dont know if this was a one off case or our choice of items was poor or the staff was overwhelmed on a Saturday night or was it just the normal standard here but the fact remains that we were truly disappointed 😔 by the experience.

featured_reviews.name: Chirag Patel
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently revisited this upscale Chinese restaurant for brunch, despite previous underwhelming experiences. Unfortunately, the lack of natural light and overuse of tacky blue lights remained a major turnoff. The ambiance, while appealing to some, doesn’t  resonate with me.
The food, while reasonably priced during brunch, didn't change my opinion about Chinese cuisine in Bombay. It still feels like a generic Chinese restaurant in a five-star hotel.

On a positive note, the staff was attentive and well-trained, with noticeably more staff members on deck. The addition of a smoking cabin upstairs was convenient, and the toned-down music was a welcome change. The unlimited flow of good brand cocktails was a great value.

While this restaurant still isn't my favorite, I appreciate the positive changes in price, smoking area, and music volume.

featured_reviews.name: Pratik K. Mody
featured_reviews.review_text:
Nom Nom is such a vibe!

The ambience really stands out! That warm, dim lighting sets the perfect mood for an intimate dinner without feeling too “try-hard.” It’s the kind of place where you naturally slow down, settle in, and actually enjoy the evening.
The food, overall, was really good and definitely amps up the experience. That said, I’d love to see a wider variety of sushi and noodle dishes on the menu. The bao bun was a bit on the chewy side, and the filling-to-bun ratio felt slightly off (could’ve used more filling). The silken tofu, though was an absolute standout. It genuinely melted in the mouth and was a wow dish, even if I wish the portion was a little more generous. The peach iced tea was perfect. Dessert-wise, the mango sticky rice could’ve been better, it felt a bit like mango purée with pieces and rice, missing that coconut-y flavour and crunch (both of which are not very difficult to crack).
Definitely a spot I’d come back to (and happily recommend) when I’m in the mood for a relaxed, date-night style dinner.

An Unforgettable Asian Dining Experience in the Heart of Khar!
If you're looking for a restaurant that delivers on every front — breathtaking interiors, extraordinary food, and an experience that lingers long after the meal — look no further than PF Chang's, Khar. This place is an absolute gem, and my recent visit left me completely blown away.

The moment you step inside PF Chang's, you're transported into a world of stunning elegance. The interiors are nothing short of spectacular — a seamless blend of contemporary design and rich Asian-inspired aesthetics. From the dramatic lighting and intricate décor to the beautifully curated artwork and warm, inviting tones, every corner of this restaurant is Instagram-worthy. The space feels luxurious yet comfortable, making it perfect for a romantic date night, a family celebration, or a fun outing with friends. It's the kind of place where the ambiance alone is worth the visit.

Now, let's talk about the food — because PF Chang's truly takes Asian cuisine to another level. The menu is a love letter to the flavors of Asia, and every dish we tried was an absolute revelation. The dishes were bursting with bold, authentic flavors, perfectly balanced with the right amount of spice, sweetness, and umami. The portions were generous, the ingredients were fresh, and the presentation was exquisite. From the starters to the mains, each plate was crafted with care and culinary finesse. This is Asian food at its absolute finest!

The staff were warm, professional, and genuinely passionate about making your dining experience special. The team was attentive without being intrusive, and their knowledge of the menu made ordering an enjoyable experience in itself.
Overall, PF Chang's in Khar, Mumbai is a world-class dining destination that truly lives up to its global reputation. It's not just a meal — it's an experience. If you haven't visited yet, you're seriously missing out. This is one restaurant I will be returning to again and again without hesitation.
Highly recommended — a perfect 10/10! 🥢✨

Royal China is the kind of place that makes you feel underdressed even when you are dressed well.

The ambience is classy without trying too hard, dim lighting, elegant interiors, and the sort of atmosphere where people suddenly start speaking 20 percent softer. It has that proper fine dining energy where even the water arrives looking expensive.

The food absolutely holds up to the reputation. The menu is extensive, packed with authentic Chinese dishes that actually taste refined instead of just aggressively spicy. The dim sums are a standout, and the overall quality of ingredients is noticeable from the first bite itself.

Service is polished and attentive without hovering over your table every two minutes asking if “everything is okay.” They know what they are doing, which makes the whole experience feel smooth.

Yes, it is expensive. The bill arrives with enough confidence to remind you this is not your local takeaway spot. But unlike many overpriced fine dining places, this one at least gives you the feeling that your money went somewhere meaningful.

Final verdict: Elegant, reliable, and consistently good. Come for the food, stay for the feeling of temporarily having your life together.

featured_reviews.name: Javed Akhtar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Here’s a full review in your signature tone, covering the Torii experience:

⸻

Torii, Bandra – Big on Vibe, Big on Bill, Bigger on Taste

When your group of diners ranges from sushi scholars to soy sauce dabblers, you need a place that checks all boxes. Torii in Bandra came highly recommended—and spoiler alert—it almost lives up to the hype, and then some.

Let’s start from the outside: that black-and-white arched entrance with the gold-lettered TORII feels like you’re about to enter a movie set. Inside, the vibe is unmistakably plush—with mirrored ceilings, retro lampshades, opulent seating, and music that doesn’t scream at you but keeps the energy flowing. It’s where Japanese zen meets Mumbai glam.

The Meal
We were 7. The table bill read ₹45,999, so yes, about ₹6.5K per head after taxes and service, but here’s what made it feel worth it:
•	Cold Young Coconut Carpaccio – Sounds fancy and tasted the part. Light, tropical, and a perfect start.
•	Miso Black Cod – Showstopper dish. Silky, melt-in-mouth. It’s what black cod dreams are made of.
•	Chicken Chilli Oil & Lemongrass Chicken Tsukune – Packed flavour bombs. The chilli oil was a standout.
•	Cold Prawns Tempura Maki – Crisp, clean, and a hit with everyone at the table.
•	Twilight Tingles (mocktail) – Refreshing and not sugary, a tough balance to nail.
•	Torii X-mess Sundae – The name may be cheeky, but this dessert brought childlike joy with its waffle castle presentation. The kind of ending you photograph before devouring.

Service
Smooth, attentive, and non-intrusive. Our server knew the menu well and paced the meal right. That’s half the job done in high-end dining.

What Could Be Better?
Not much honestly. A couple of small hits and misses on portion sizes (looking at you, gyoza), but hey, we weren’t here for the quantity.
The bill might jolt you for a second, but by the end of the night, you’ll justify it to yourself with, “Well, the black cod made up for it.”

My final two bit

Paise gaye, par taste ban gaya.

Aide  dessert  pe toh calories bhi selfie mangti hai.

📍 Final Verdict:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ — A strong 5 stars for a place that brings together design, service, and standout dishes under one gilded roof. For special dinners, date nights, or flex-worthy Instagram reels, Torii hits the spot..

The blue pea flower fried rice with smoked chicken was the star of the meal, beautifully smoky and absolutely delicious. I wish we could have one more serving of it.

We ended the ordeal with the ice cream brownie sizzler, which was outstanding with its rich caramel sauce and perfect balance of textures.

featured_reviews.review_text:
BLUE’S Thai Kitchen serves excellent Thai food, and it’s a place I genuinely love. I’ve visited multiple times over the last 4–5 years, and the food quality has remained consistently great. Chef Loima at times chats and recommends some dishes to try.

The restaurant is quite small, with around six tables accommodating roughly 20 people, so it can feel cramped. Despite this, the service is super fast, and the team works efficiently to manage the crowd.

One piece of feedback, the owner (often present) tends to stand very close to tables or hover around, which can feel uncomfortable. Regardless of the waiting outside, customers come for the experience and should be allowed to sit, relax, and enjoy their meal without feeling rushed or watched or someone being very direct or rude.

Apart from this, everything else is excellent. Still a highly recommended spot for authentic Thai food.

The food is delicious, no-nonsense good. The Dragon roll sushi is fresh and tasty, the Hamachi with Ponzo could be better. The pork belly bao is soft, the meat tender, and the flavour, spot-on. The spicy prawn Donburi is a burst of smoky spicy flavours and the mini pork ramen, just as comforting as a ramen should be with 2 large strips of pork. Both, highly recommended! And even if you feel uncomfortable (which I did), they will not let you move to a better table. We went in early, yet were made to sit in a cramped corner beside the bar and washroom which made it quite noisy and not the best seats. This was our second visit, and on both occasions the restaurant acted out with the seating
Second, you are on the Conde Nast list, the basic serving etiquette that is expected is that you don’t pile all the food together on the table. One can ask the patron whether everything is expected in one go or simply bring the food as different courses. Sadly, not at Mizu!

featured_reviews.name: Prakash Dhalwani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mizu has quickly become one of my favorite spots in Bombay. The vibe is super calming and minimal, with a beautiful setup that makes you want to just sit back and enjoy a long, relaxed meal.

We ordered the salmon roll, prawn sushi, asparagus sushi, and both chicken and veg gyoza—and honestly, everything was incredible. The salmon roll was so fresh and perfectly balanced, and the prawn sushi had just the right amount of flavor without being overpowering. Even the asparagus sushi (which I wasn’t expecting much from) turned out to be a standout—super clean and fresh-tasting.

The gyozas were spot on too—crispy on the bottom, juicy inside, and served with a dipping sauce that really tied it all together. You can tell they really care about the quality of ingredients and presentation.

Drinks were great (highly recommend trying one of their signature cocktails), and the service was warm and helpful without hovering. It’s definitely on the pricier side, but for the quality of food, the ambiance, and the overall experience, I’d say it’s totally worth it.

Already looking forward to going back!

featured_reviews.name: TheLefty Prodigy
featured_reviews.review_text: I had such an amazing experience. Everything from the sushis to ramen was top notch. Loved the pork broth, the katsu chicken rolls, the chicken gyoza, the non-alcoholic cocktails and the desserts! Especially the desserts! The server was Joshua who was exceptional! Always smiling and super friendly. ❤️

featured_reviews.name: Swati Pillai
featured_reviews.review_text:
Overpriced, overhyped, and shockingly arrogant

Mizu is sold as a top luxury restaurant in Mumbai, with visits from celebrities and the affluent, but the experience last night was a complete letdown.

Even the interiors felt like a missed opportunity, far from the polished, premium vibe the pricing suggests.

We spent ₹17,600+ on small plates and drinks, and most of the food was average at best, nothing you wouldn’t get at a regular Asian restaurant.

The service was HORRENDOUS.
We were warned three times before arriving that we must vacate the table by 9:30 PM, and then reminded multiple times again during dinner. It felt like we were being rushed out from the moment we sat down.

Service was slow and sloppy, and we had to constantly ask them to clear used plates and bowls. They even forgot our order. We were even asked repeatedly to return the menu, as if they don’t have enough menus to run a “premium” restaurant.

The most unbelievable part: when my friend considered ordering another glass of wine, the steward (Vijay) actually said, “It’s better you don’t order.”

For a place charging these prices, the attitude is unacceptable. The service is abysmal.
Mizu cares more about table turnover than hospitality. What makes such places arrogant in an Indian city with a culture that is driven with hospitality and warmth?
Never again, Mizu. I’m taking my hard-earned money where the service, atmosphere, food quality, and overall experience is commensurate!

featured_reviews.name: JASON SEQUEIRA
featured_reviews.review_text:
🍣 Mizu – Bandra Review 🍜

Had an amazing dining experience at Mizu Bandra, one of those places that perfectly blends cozy vibes with top-notch Japanese cuisine. The ambiance is modern, minimal, and effortlessly elegant — perfect for both a casual outing or a special dinner. ✨

Here’s what I tried:

🍣 Salmon and Prawn Rolls – absolutely fresh and flavorful! The rolls were perfectly rolled, with the right balance of rice, seafood, and seasoning. The texture was spot on, and every bite just melted in the mouth. Easily one of the highlights of the meal!

🥟 Gyozas – crispy on the outside, juicy on the inside. These dumplings were packed with flavor and served hot, making them the perfect appetizer.

🍜 Ramen – rich, flavorful, and comforting. The broth was hearty and aromatic, the noodles cooked just right, and the toppings perfectly balanced — truly authentic and satisfying.

🍛 Golden Curry – such a comforting dish! Creamy, flavorful, and mildly spiced with that signature Japanese curry richness. It’s the kind of dish that just warms you up instantly.

🍗 Chicken Rice Bowl – tender, well-marinated chicken served over fluffy rice — simple, hearty, and full of flavor. Perfect for anyone who loves balanced, wholesome bowls.

Everything at Mizu was beautifully presented and tasted even better than it looked. The service was friendly and attentive, adding to the overall experience. If you’re in Bandra and craving authentic Japanese flavors with a modern twist, Mizu is definitely the place to go.

featured_reviews.name: Mita Biswas
featured_reviews.review_text: Easily one of the best Japanese dining experiences in Mumbai! The ramen broth here is incredibly rich and comforting, absolute perfection. We loved the Edamame Truffle Gyoza and the Softshell Crab Roll, both packed with flavor and beautifully presented. The vibe is lively and sophisticated, making it an amazing spot for a special night out. The staff was incredibly warm and helpful with recommendations. Don't skip dessert; the Japanese cheesecake is a must! Make sure to book a table well in advance.

On the positive side, the Tiger Fries were absolutely fabulous—perfectly done and very enjoyable. The Takoyaki chicken was okayish, but there’s room for improvement.

featured_reviews.name: Smridhi Sharma

We tried the spicy cottage cheese with noodles, vegetable pan-seared gyoza, and tofu katsu curry — and honestly, everything was on point. The spice was perfectly balanced, the noodles were super satisfying, and the gyoza had that ideal crispy-soft texture.

The sides added a nice fresh contrast, and the tofu katsu curry was rich and comforting. What made the experience even better was the warm, attentive service and the music, which really elevated the whole vibe. Wasim and Azhar were top notch with their service.

Overall, great food, great energy, and definitely a place worth going back to.

featured_reviews.name: Aniket
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tiger Yaki is an absolute hidden gem near Carter Road, Bandra, serving excellent Japanese and Korean food. It’s a no-fuss place with indoor AC and outdoor seating, where food is served in takeaway-style boxes and bowls. We visited as a group of six, including two kids, and loved everything we ordered—corn dog, veg and mushroom gyoza, tofu katsu curry, and mushroom and prawn takoyaki. The food was fresh, delicious, reasonably priced, service was excellent, toilets are available, though parking can be tricky.

Getting a good seat can be a challenge if you’re in a group of 4 and above. The indoor setting can sit just about 7 to 8 people so most of the times you’ll have to sit outside and face the heat and mosquitoes.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Jim Me's Kitchen for some classic desi Chinese, and it turned out to be a pretty solid budget-friendly spot.

The food was good for the price, with really generous portion sizes that make it feel completely worth it. We tried the pork chilly, which was actually quite good, along with their triple Schezwan fried rice — mild spicy, filling, and perfect if you enjoy proper Indo-Chinese comfort food. The flavors overall were decent and satisfying without trying to be overly fancy.

The ambience is very simple and lowkey — old interiors, wooden benches, and a very no-frills vibe. It’s definitely more about the food than the aesthetics, but that old-school charm kind of adds to the experience.

Another big plus is the pricing. Two people can easily have a full meal here for under ₹1.5k, which is great considering the quantity they serve. Overall, a good spot in Bandra for affordable and comforting desi Chinese.

Had a lovely dining experience at Foo. The overall food quality was impressive, and you can really tell that a lot of attention is given to presentation and flavour’s and service
The sushi was extremely fresh and beautifully plated — definitely one of the highlights of the meal. The dim sums were equally amazing, soft, well-seasoned, and perfectly steamed. Every dish we tried had great balance and authenticity, which made the experience even more enjoyable.
However, I was slightly disappointed with the Picante cocktail I ordered. It didn’t taste like a typical picante — the flavor was quite bland and lacked the spicy kick and boldness that you usually expect. It could definitely be improved to match the overall standard of the food.
Overall, it was a very good experience with excellent food, especially the sushi and dim sums. With a slight improvement in the cocktail, it would be absolutely perfect. Would definitely visit again!

featured_reviews.name: Gaurav Suri
featured_reviews.review_text:
Foo Bandra truly knows how to turn a meal into an experience. From the moment you walk in, the ambiance sets the tone — stylish yet relaxed, perfect for a long, lingering lunch or an intimate dinner.

We ordered the Hot & Sour Soup with tofu and broccoli, Spicy Chicken Dimsum, Foo Wild Salmon Umaraki (a delightful mix of rice, avocado, salmon, guacamole, and spicy cream sauce), Blue Butter Japanese Rice, and Hakka Chicken with mushrooms, scallions, and ginger. Every dish was beautifully presented and full of flavor — fresh ingredients, balanced textures, and just the right amount of spice.

The highlight was how effortlessly the afternoon flowed — great food, warm service, and conversations that stretched over 2.5 hours without feeling rushed. We ended on a sweet note with the Snickerz Nut Crunch — rich, indulgent, and the perfect finish.

featured_reviews.name: Suyash Karangutkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re a fan of bold flavors and comforting desi Chinese, Fat Kong is the kind of place that satisfies every craving with just the right hit of spice, crunch, and umami.

Crispy Chicken:
This dish was a knockout. The chicken pieces were perfectly battered—thin, golden, and fried to a shatteringly crisp texture. The outside had that addictive crunch, while the inside stayed juicy and tender. Tossed in a sticky, mildly spicy glaze with hints of garlic, soy, and chili, it was garnished with spring onions and sesame seeds, making it hard to stop at just one piece.

Chicken Triple Rice & Schezwan Noodles:
The Chicken Triple Rice was a full-on flavor bomb—a mix of fried rice and schezwan gravy poured generously on top, loaded with chopped veggies, chicken chunks, and a fried egg to top it all off. It was hearty, spicy, and soul-satisfying in that uniquely desi-Chinese way.

The Schezwan Noodles had a perfect wok-char (you know that smoky “wok hei” touch), with the right chewiness and a punchy garlic-chili flavor that didn’t overpower. Again, the chicken pieces were soft and well-seasoned, blending nicely with the heat of the schezwan sauce and the crunch of stir-fried vegetables.

It was one of those restaurants where we visited every weekend and it was always full so we had to wait 15 to 20 mins to get a table, and it was worth the wait.

So after around a decade I decided to revisit this restaurant for nostalgia and to try their iconic starters which made me drool earlier on.

So they are having two outlets now Jogeshwari and Khar, I visited the Khar outlet and was happy to see the restaurant maintaining their yellow and red colour theme. I was the only one present in their restaurant and was greeted by Akshay the person managing this outlet.

After requesting that I wish to try 2 dishes he was kind enough to give me 1/2 portion of my favourite Chicken Lollipop Hakka Style and Full portion of Crispy Spinach Chicken.

As soon as the lollipops were served the aroma transported me to the old era it was so beautiful and they have done well to maintain their taste as it was before.

But now comes the sad part, I got a piece of plastic spoon in my mouth while having the dish and was angry, disappointed and sad. I was advised by some of my friends that I should avoid the restaurant as it's not maintained the same way like before, but still I decided to try and I was like this is the end of Fatkongs for me.

I requested the Manager to not charge me for this dish and speak to the owner regarding this but he was helpless and they decided not to take away the charges.

The spinach didn't seem fresh and the chicken had a thick coating and wasn't good. So with a heavy heart I left the restaurant putting down a message to the owner who did give me a call and tried to give explanation and reasoning, though admitting that it wasn't right. featured_reviews.name: saumya poddar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Goh jia Ting - restaurant in bandra, had been on our list for a while, so after a show, we decided to finally give it a try. To be honest, walking into an almost empty restaurant was a little concerning. We were only the second occupied table, and the place remained virtually vacant throughout our visit. Still, we were extremely hungry and the overwhelmingly positive reviews online convinced us to stay and order.

Unfortunately, things went downhill from there.

One of the strangest parts of the evening was the service. At one point, a staff member stood directly in front of our table, watching us eat for an uncomfortably long time. It wasn’t attentive service—it felt intrusive and awkward. She only moved after we specifically requested her to. It genuinely made us uncomfortable, as though we were being monitored rather than hosted.

When I requested disposable chopsticks, the staff said they had them but then handed me what looked like a stranded stirrers and then later confessed that they don’t have disposable chopstick, then why say yes at the first place. Super careless and unprofessional.

The food was even worse. The prawn tempura roll tasted like it had been fried in old, stale oil. Instead of gyoza, we were served something that resembled chicken momos. The lobster roll was completely inedible and was left untouched after a few bites.

The cocktail we ordered, made with star fruit, was equally disappointing. It was so bad that we replaced it with a simple whisky just to avoid any more unpleasant surprises.

After struggling through the starters, we decided not to risk ordering anything else and left for another restaurant to have dinner. The entire experience felt like a complete waste of money.

What started as a restaurant we were genuinely excited to try ended up being one of the most disappointing dining experiences we’ve had in Bandra. Between the awkward service, poor food quality, disappointing drinks, and overall lacklustre experience, we left wondering how the glowing reviews online could possibly reflect what we experienced.

There are far too many great dining options in Bandra to spend your time and money here.

Dynasty: The Indo-Chinese Restaurant That Doesn’t Need Buzz
Five stars aren’t enough, but they’ll have to do.
Dynasty operates in that rare territory where quality speaks louder than Instagram followers. This unpretentious neighborhood spot has mastered the art of authentic Indo-Chinese cooking — the kind that requires skill, not shortcuts.
Order the Chicken Lollipop and you’ll understand immediately. Each piece is a study in balance: crisp exterior, succulent interior, perfectly seasoned. The Manchow Soup arrives with the kind of umami depth that makes you wonder why other restaurants even bother. The Crispy Spinach Chicken demands respect, while the Crispy Thread Chicken delivers texture with purpose. These aren’t interpretations — they’re the genuine article.
But the real revelation lies in the Sour Chili and Sichuan dips. Layered, bold, and unapologetically complex, they’re the kind of accompaniments that transform a meal into an experience. The lemon iced tea cuts through it all with perfect timing.
What distinguishes Dynasty, though, is the service. The team moves with purpose, never intrusive, always present. It’s a family restaurant in the truest sense — one that makes you feel like you belong.
In a city saturated with forgettable Indo-Chinese, Dynasty reminds you why authenticity never goes out of style.

Dynasty Restaurant, Khar West: A Chinese Culinary Journey

Dynasty Restaurant in Khar West, Mumbai, is a haven for Chinese food enthusiasts. This popular eatery has been delighting taste buds with its authentic and flavorful dishes for years. Whether you're craving spicy, tangy, or sweet, Dynasty has something to offer.

One of the must-try dishes at Dynasty is their Crispy Spinach Paneer. This vegetarian delight features tender cubes of paneer coated in a crispy batter and tossed with fresh spinach. The combination of textures and flavors is simply irresistible. For a refreshing drink to complement your meal, try their Ice Lemon Tea. The tartness of the lemon combined with the sweetness of the tea makes it a perfect thirst quencher.

If you're looking for something spicy, the Paneer Chilli is a great option. Tender pieces of paneer are stir-fried with a spicy chili sauce, making it a fiery dish that will leave your taste buds tingling. For a unique twist on Chinese cuisine, try the Schezwan Crispy Veg. This dish features mixed vegetables coated in a crispy batter and tossed in a spicy Schezwan sauce.

For a satisfying main course, consider the Veg Burnt Garlic Rice or the Veg Malaysian Noodles. Both dishes are packed with flavor and are sure to leave you feeling full and satisfied. Dynasty also offers a variety of Indian Chinese dishes, combining traditional Indian flavors with Chinese cooking techniques.

To start your meal, the Manchow Soup is a classic choice. This flavorful soup is packed with vegetables and a hint of spice. For a refreshing and tangy drink, try the Sweet and Salty Lime Soda. The combination of sweet and salty flavors is a unique and refreshing treat.

Whether you're a seasoned Chinese food lover or new to the cuisine, Dynasty Restaurant in Khar West is a must-visit. With its delicious food, friendly service, and inviting atmosphere, it's no wonder why this restaurant is so popular among locals and tourists alike.
